soundness_flags.label: ass:lag-one-nonanticipation
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited nonanticipation condition excludes future assignments but permits arbitrary dependence on the whole past; the stated equality for histories agreeing only at t-1 and t is a stronger finite-memory/lag-one restriction and must be retagged or separately sourced.

soundness_flags.label: thm:projection-covariance consumer
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed pre-deployment screening by an observable balance direction is unsupported: P depends on beta_b and hence on unobserved potential-outcome scores a_gb, while no observable estimator or proxy for P is defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-design-clt, thm:studentizer, thm:wald-coverage
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: These are conditional on the explicitly assumed predictable covariance stabilization and positive-definite limit, rather than claiming that those finite-population regularities follow from boundedness alone.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Root-GB normality and conservative simultaneous coverage hold under ass:rr-covariance-stabilization and ass:rr-limit-positive, together with the stated design assumptions.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:projection-covariance
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The limiting comparison is conditional on complete-randomization covariance and projection stabilization.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The covariance-gain identity holds under ass:cr-covariance-stabilization and ass:projection-stabilization; it does not claim to derive existence of Omega_CR or P from the design alone.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Its nonanticipation assumption restricts outcomes only against future assignments and states that arbitrary dependence on past and contemporaneous assignments remains allowed.
The paper establishes finite-population IPW/AIPW theory for general adaptive designs and explicitly includes sequential rerandomization among its applications.
The paper proposes a minimax design jointly addressing spillover and carryover effects, studies HT asymptotic normality, and proposes conservative variance estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: PMC rendering of the published PNAS 115 (2018) article; PNAS primary page was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article analyzes static rerandomization in a treatment-control experiment through the joint asymptotic distribution of the ATE and covariate imbalance.
The article supplies unbiased estimators for direct and spillover quantities and conservative variance estimators in a general static two-stage randomized-experiment setting.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2209.12345v4, 12 June 2025; corroborating version of the subsequently published AoS article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives Stein-method Berry-Esseen bounds for linear permutation statistics and quadratic functions of their estimators.
The paper develops Stein-method Berry-Esseen bounds for heterogeneous stratified linear permutation statistics.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2301.09016v7, 15 January 2026; corroborating version of the cited Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies two-stage covariate-adaptive randomization under homogeneous partial interference and derives consistency, asymptotic normality, and asymptotic variance estimators for primary and spillover effects.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag ass:lag-one-nonanticipation as a novel finite-memory restriction, explain why two-period held assignments make it empirically credible, or replace it with a source that actually imposes lag-one memory.
Either remove the claim that c'Pc is screenable before deployment or define an observable, logged-data estimator or ex ante proxy for P and add its consistency/decision guarantee.

Add a finite-G worked calculation for the completed covariance matrix under a nonconstant adaptive history and state precisely which PSD property is proved for the raw completion versus obtained only by spectral clipping.

recommended_next_step: Revise the lag-one assumption and the claimed observability of the projection criterion, then retain the field-tier adaptive soft-rerandomization kernel for Stage 0.
